title: Use a CSPRNG file key for AES-256 encryption and preserve /Info on protect
acceptance: cargo test -p pdfxi-security; two protects of the same source with the same passwords produce different file keys, and an independent reader opens the result while /Info survives
notes: Follow-up from the orchestrator's review of T-0238 (docs/evidence/hardening/T-0238.md, Known limitations). Three defects, recorded as cryptographic-quality issues to fix before release, not as an exploitable-today claim. 1) The existing writer derives the AES-256 file key deterministically from the document /ID plus the user and owner passwords (derive_file_key in encryption_writer.rs) instead of drawing a random 32-byte file key and wrapping it through /UE and /OE per ISO 32000-2 revision 6. A shared/deterministic key is a real weakness: replace it with a CSPRNG (vetted getrandom/rand, licence-checked), generate the R6 salts and validation values per spec, and add a test that two protects of identical bytes and passwords yield different /UE, /OE, /U, /O and /Perms-derived values. 2) protect and remove-protection emit a minimal trailer (Size, Root, ID, Encrypt) and lose the /Info reference; preserve /Info (and any other trailer keys that do not conflict) in protected and decrypted output. 3) Independent-reader verification is missing: the T-0238 tests reopen with the same crate that wrote the file. Add a PDFium reopen (with the password; failure without it) and, where available, a second reader (qpdf or Adobe) so the file is not validated only by its author. Rows stay library until the shell task; do not promote anything here.
